title: Foundations: Starlight Lullabies - The Complete Guide
summary: What Starlight Lullabies is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Starlight Lullabies songs: Lullabies are humanity's oldest songs: soft, repetitive melodies sung to ease children into sleep. Every culture has them; the best use rocking rhythms and simple, soothing words.

History: Brahms's Wiegenlied (1868) is the classical lullaby; Rock-a-Bye Baby (1884) and Twinkle Twinkle (1806) are the English-language standards. Lullabies predate all other song forms.

How the songs work: Starlight Lullabies favors the keys of C, F, G, Bb. Common forms include Short verses repeated with slight variation; Hummed refrains. Players should master 6/8 rocking rhythm like a cradle first, then soft dynamics throughout; no surprises. Gentle fingerpicking; soft capo optional.

title: Rock-a-Bye Baby - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Rock-a-Bye Baby, a public-domain Starlight Lullabies standard.
body:
Rock-a-Bye Baby (Effie I. Canning, 1884. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Rock-a-bye baby, in the treetop,
When the wind blows, the cradle will rock.
When the bough breaks, the cradle will fall,
And down will come baby, cradle and all.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Starlight Lullabies accompaniment in C using the 'Cradle I–V–I' pattern:
C | G | C | F

Technique: 6/8 rocking rhythm like a cradle. Gentle fingerpicking; soft capo optional.
